title: Charts, histograms, box plots
examples: How do I know which scale to use for my histogram?
What is the difference between a bar chart and a histogram?
Can I use box plots to compare more than two sets of data?

explain.say: Today we are looking at charts to show data. We will learn about histograms and box plots. These help us compare different sets of numbers.
A histogram uses bars to show how often data falls into groups. The area of the bar is important here. We calculate frequency density for each bar.
Frequency density is the height of the bar, but it is adjusted. It shows the frequency spread over the class width. For example, if ten students scored between ten and twenty, the density is one.
Box plots help us compare the spread and centre of data easily. We look at the minimum, the median, and the maximum values. This gives a quick picture of the spread.
When comparing two box plots, we check where the median lines are. We also compare the length of the boxes to see which data set is more spread out.

Imagine you are tracking the heights of students in your class. You could use a histogram to see how many students fall into height groups like five feet to five feet six inches. This shows the spread of heights in your group.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bar chart and a histogram?
faq.a: A bar chart uses separate gaps between bars for different categories. A histogram uses touching bars to show continuous numerical data ranges.
asks: When should I use a histogram instead of a bar chart?
Are the bars in a histogram always touching?

faq.q: Why do I need to calculate frequency density?
faq.a: We use frequency density because the class intervals on the x-axis are not always the same width. It makes the comparison fair.
asks: What is the purpose of frequency density?
Does frequency density help me compare different groups?

faq.q: What does the median show on a box plot?
faq.a: The median is the middle value when all the data points are lined up in order. It divides the data into two equal halves.
asks: How do I find the middle number in a box plot?
Is the median always the mean?

faq.q: What does the length of the box tell me?
faq.a: The length of the box shows the middle fifty percent of your data. A longer box means the middle data is more spread out.
asks: What does the interquartile range represent?
How spread out is the middle half of the data?

faq.q: Can I compare three or more sets of data?
faq.a: Yes, you can compare many sets of data. You would draw a separate box plot for each set you are comparing.
asks: Is it okay to compare more than two groups?
What if I have four different data sets to compare?

facts: A histogram uses touching bars to represent continuous data.
Frequency density is calculated by dividing the frequency by the class width.
The median is the value that splits a data set exactly in half.
A box plot shows the minimum, the median, and the maximum values easily.

quiz.say: If a class interval is from five to fifteen, what is the class width?
quiz.why: The width is found by subtracting the lower limit from the upper limit.

wrong.0: This is the starting point, not the total spread.
wrong.1: This is the ending point, not the total spread.
wrong.2: You cannot add the two numbers together to find the width.

quiz.say: A box plot shows the middle fifty percent using which part?
quiz.show: The box shows Q1 to Q3
quiz.why: The box stretches from the first quartile to the third quartile.

wrong.0: The range is only the difference between the highest and lowest points.
wrong.2: That line represents the median, which is only one point.
wrong.3: The whiskers show the minimum and maximum, not the middle fifty percent.

quiz.say: If a data set has a median of twenty and a range of forty, what is the minimum value if the maximum is sixty?
quiz.why: You subtract the range from the maximum value to find the minimum.

wrong.0: You cannot subtract the median from the range to find the minimum.
wrong.2: This is the range itself, not the minimum value.
wrong.3: You should not add the range and the maximum together.
